reason: The spec (issue #1, open, v0.54.0) is concrete and the codebase already has every seam it names: a verbspec CLI (tokens/cli.ts) with a `check` verb that shells to tokens/check.ts, a standalone gate (check.ts) that runs the two dogfood checks, two built mocks with index.html + style.css (tokens/examples/mock-orange, mock-blue), and a CI workflow (.github/workflows/tokens-check.yml) that runs check.ts per brand. The tezcatl + axe-core injection pattern is already implemented in the org's conformance-kit (gates/axe-gate.mjs, `AXE_RUNNER=tezcatl`, `tezcatl <url> --wait=N --eval=...`) so the mechanism is proven and can be ported to Deno in ~100 lines. The main design decision is where the browser runs in CI: tezcatl is macOS-native WebKit via a Nix flake, but tokens-check.yml runs on ubuntu-latest, so the axe step needs either a second macos-14 job with nix-installer (the pattern site-ci.yml's `browser` job already uses) or a Playwright/Chromium fallback runner. Not verifiable in this sandbox: deno is not installed, no browser, no tezcatl.
current_state: Repo @ be917d0 (v0.54.0). Root is the Node/mjs site-build engine; the task lives entirely under tokens/ (Deno 2, deno.json imports zod + jsr:@bounded-systems/verbspec, deno.lock present, no axe-core/tezcatl anywhere in the lock). Relevant files: tokens/cli.ts (verbspec registry: seed-palette, style, build, check; `checkVerb` runs check.ts via `runScript`; exits 1 when output.ok===false); tokens/check.ts (re-derives via to-css.ts + to-tokens.ts into a temp dir, byte-compares style.css/tokens.dtcg.json/tokens.sd.json, then runs audit.ts and cvd-hues.ts as subprocesses, prints `check <out>: drift ✓ · audit ✓ · cvd ✓`, exits 0/1); tokens/audit.ts (full-indirection), tokens/cvd-hues.ts (1.4.1), tokens/derive.ts (derivation), tokens/build-brand.ts. Built mocks: tokens/examples/mock-orange/{index.html,style.css,tokens.dtcg.json,tokens.sd.json} and tokens/examples/mock-blue/ (same set), plus tokens/examples/mock/{index.html,style.css}; index.html is a small hand-written page (h1/p/a/h2/article.card/h3/button/small, lang=en, title, links ./style.css) not touched since v0.51.0. CI: .github/workflows/tokens-check.yml (ubuntu-latest, setup-deno v2.x, `deno check *.ts`, then `deno run --allow-read --allow-write --allow-run check.ts brands/burnt-orange/brand.json examples/mock-orange` and the deep-blue equivalent; path-filtered to tokens/**). .github/workflows/site-ci.yml already has a `browser` job on macos-14 with DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action running `AXE_RUNNER=tezcatl nix shell github:bdelanghe/tezcatl-flake -c node .conformance-kit/gates/axe-gate.mjs dist` — the exact provisioning recipe to copy. BROWSER.md documents the tezcatl-on-macOS policy. External reference impl: bounded-systems/conformance-kit gates/axe-gate.mjs (depends on axe-core ^4.10; startServer() serves dist over ephemeral localhost, injects `<script src=/__axe-core.js>` + an axe.run() that writes results into a `<script type=application/json id=__axe_results>` node; tezcatl is invoked as `tezcatl <url> --wait=<ms> --eval=<js reading that node>`, retried once with 2x wait). No axe verb, no axe.ts, no a11y step exists in synoptic today. Only `deno task check` exists for the gate; no test harness for a negative (injected-violation) case.
plan: 1. tokens/deno.json — add `"axe-core": "npm:axe-core@^4.10"` to imports (so `import.meta.resolve`/`Deno.readTextFile` can locate axe.min.js from the npm cache; alternatively vendor axe.min.js under tokens/vendor/ and commit it — pick the one that keeps deno.lock reproducible). Regenerate tokens/deno.lock.

2. tokens/axe.ts (new) — the gate script, mirroring conformance-kit's tezcatl runner in Deno: (a) `Deno.serve` outDir on 127.0.0.1:0 with axe.min.js served at /__axe-core.js and the runner snippet appended before </body> of any .html; (b) for each *.html in outDir run `new Deno.Command(Deno.env.get('TEZCATL') ?? 'tezcatl', { args: [url, '--wait=' + wait, '--eval=<read #__axe_results>'] })`, retry once with 2x wait; (c) parse `{violations}`, run tags wcag2a/wcag2aa/wcag21a/wcag21aa/wcag22aa, assert `violations.length === 0` (issue says ZERO, not impact-thresholded); print one summary line `axe <outDir>: N pages · 0 violations ✓` or list id/impact/targets and exit 1. Env: AXE_TEZCATL_WAIT (default 3000), optional AXE_RUNNER=playwright fallback only if you decide to support ubuntu (see step 5). Usage: `deno run --allow-read --allow-net --allow-run --allow-env axe.ts <outDir>`.

3. tokens/cli.ts — add `axeVerb = defineVerb({ id: 'axe', summary: 'Third-party a11y: render the built mock in tezcatl (WebKit), inject axe-core, assert zero violations.', actor: 'ci', input: z.object({ out: z.string() }), output: RunResult, run: ({ out }) => runScript('axe.ts', [out]) })`, register it in `CLI`, and extend `runScript` permissions with --allow-net --allow-env (or give axe.ts its own permission list). Update the `check` verb summary to mention axe.

4. tokens/check.ts — after the audit/cvd subprocesses add `const axe = await deno([here('axe.ts'), outDir])` (using the wider permission list), include `axe.code === 0` in `ok`, print `axe: <firstLine>` and add `· axe ✓/✗` to the summary line. Decide skip semantics: if `tezcatl` is not on PATH, fail (fail-closed, consistent with the repo's posture) unless `AXE_SKIP=1` is set explicitly — document it in the header comment.

5. .github/workflows/tokens-check.yml — the existing `check` job runs on ubuntu-latest where tezcatl cannot run. Either (recommended, matches BROWSER.md/site-ci.yml) add a second job `axe` on macos-14: checkout (SHA-pinned), setup-deno, DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@<SHA> (copy the pin from site-ci.yml), then `nix shell github:bdelanghe/tezcatl-flake -c deno run --allow-read --allow-net --allow-run --allow-env cli.ts axe --out examples/mock-orange` and the mock-blue equivalent; and keep the ubuntu job's check.ts invocation with AXE_SKIP=1 (or move the check.ts calls to the macOS job so check.ts runs all four gates in one place). Or move the whole `check` job to macos-14. Keep all actions SHA-pinned per org policy (PR #6 established this for this workflow).

6. tokens/GROUNDING.md / root LAYERS.md or CORE.md — one line noting the tokens layer now carries a third-party axe gate (CORE.md currently says the tezcatl browser job is 'opt-in, off, until it's cheap' — update or scope that statement).

7. Negative proof for the verify criterion: add a fixture or a documented one-liner that injects a violation into a copy of a mock (e.g. `sed 's/lang="en"//' examples/mock-orange/index.html` or removing the , or adding `<img src=x>` without alt) into a temp dir alongside style.css, runs `cli.ts axe --out <tmp>`, and asserts exit 1. Optionally encode this as tokens/axe.test.ts guarded on tezcatl being on PATH so `deno test` covers both directions.

8. Bump package.json version (v0.55.0) and tag per the repo's convention (commits are `feat: … (vX.Y.Z)`). PR must reference `Closes #1` for the pr-claim check, and CLAUDE.md requires claiming the issue via claim-ticket.yml first.
verify_command: cd tokens && deno run --allow-read --allow-write --allow-run --allow-net --allow-env check.ts brands/burnt-orange/brand.json examples/mock-orange && deno run --allow-read --allow-write --allow-run --allow-net --allow-env check.ts brands/deep-blue/brand.json examples/mock-blue && T=$(mktemp -d) && cp examples/mock-orange/style.css "$T/" && sed 's///; s#link##' examples/mock-orange/index.html > "$T/index.html" && if deno run --allow-read --allow-net --allow-run --allow-env cli.ts axe --out "$T"; then echo 'FAIL: axe passed an injected violation'; exit 1; else echo 'OK: axe gate failed closed on injected violation'; fi
risks: tezcatl is macOS-native WebKit (Nix flake, bdelanghe/tezcatl-flake) and tokens-check.yml runs on ubuntu-latest — the gate cannot run in the existing job; needs a macos-14 job (slower, more expensive runner) or a Playwright/Chromium fallback, which contradicts BROWSER.md's 'WebKit not Chromium' policy. Confirm the intended CI shape with the issue author before wiring.
Cannot be verified in this sandbox: no deno, no tezcatl, no browser, no nix; the verify_command only proves the criterion on a mac with tezcatl on PATH (or in the macOS CI job).

tezcatl's exact CLI (`<url> --wait=N --eval=JS`, 'NORESULT' sentinel) is inferred from conformance-kit's axe-gate.mjs; verify against the current tezcatl-flake before relying on it, and the flake's `nix shell` cold-start time may dominate the job.

README.md states 'The engine ORCHESTRATES; it never re-implements a gate' — writing a Deno axe runner duplicates conformance-kit's axe-gate.mjs. Alternative is to have axe.ts shell out to the kit's gate (`AXE_RUNNER=tezcatl AXE_IMPACT_THRESHOLD=minor node $CK_GATES/axe-gate.mjs <outDir>`), but the tokens/ layer is Deno-only today and the kit is a peerDependency; whichever is chosen should be stated in the PR.

Issue asks for zero violations, but the kit's gate blocks only at `serious`+ by default; the mock's hand-written index.html may already surface minor/moderate findings (e.g. region/landmark, heading-order) that would fail a strict zero-violation gate on main — the first run may require fixing the mock HTML, not just adding the gate.
axe's color-contrast rule can report `impact: null`/'incomplete' for elements it cannot resolve; the gate must define whether `incomplete` counts, otherwise 'zero violations' is under-specified.

Adding npm:axe-core to deno.json changes deno.lock and adds a runtime npm fetch in CI; the osv deps lane will start scanning it. Vendoring axe.min.js avoids the fetch but adds a ~500KB committed file.

Org process: CLAUDE.md requires running .claude/org-repair.sh and claiming the issue via claim-ticket.yml before working; pr-claim check requires `Closes #1` in the PR. The sandbox has no GitHub credentials so the claim step must happen elsewhere.
check.ts currently always exits non-zero on any sub-gate failure; if tezcatl is absent locally (a Linux dev box) the combined gate becomes unrunnable unless an explicit skip switch is designed in.
